items.description: Existing prepared sidecars have no explicit path to establish a concurrent-delivery relationship.
items.evidence: Existing records skip the creation step containing reciprocal-link instructions; activate and build require the link without creating it.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Allow an explicitly requested existing sidecar to be linked to a selected parent through a recoverable reciprocal update, without inferring a relationship.
items.rationale: Concurrent activation automatically establishes the reciprocal link in either order; completion resolves links according to which work is delivered.

items.description: Unsupported kinds still receive generic next actions in later lifecycle states.
items.evidence: The guard excludes only preparation states; later states fall through to the general status map.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Determine whether generic later-stage workflows apply to these kinds and constrain or diagnose unsupported routes consistently.
items.rationale: The consolidate-state-enums change will enumerate supported kinds and make unsupported kinds invalid.

items.description: The public lifecycle reference still describes the previous abbreviated workflow.
items.evidence: docs/LIFECYCLE.md retains direct bugfix/refactor execution and an outdated Mermaid transition.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Align the public reference with the current lifecycle and skill guidance, including the S-sized design path.
items.rationale: Public lifecycle documentation must reflect the implemented workflow, including abbreviated activation and the S-sized design skip.

items.description: Resolve still describes dispatching abbreviated execution via bugfix or refactor.
items.evidence: The named skill now hands off to build; the report does not establish that resolve fails to reconcile the resulting work.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Check resolve’s dispatch and reconciliation contract against the new handoff and clarify any real mismatch.
items.rationale: The authorised abbreviated workflow can delegate execution to build; no reconciliation failure was demonstrated.

items.description: The task claims verify and review guidance was reconciled although those files were not edited.
items.evidence: Neither file changed; lack of edits alone does not show that existing instructions are inconsistent.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Inspect the actual verification and review guidance and correct only demonstrable gaps or the task wording.
items.rationale: Existing verify and review support named non-selected abbreviated work; no conflicting instruction was identified.

items.description: Next-action reporting now interprets task completion in a new sidecar-specific parser.
items.evidence: The code parses Markdown tasks and fences, while normal building records report build without task inspection; progress is not proof of task completion.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Assess the parser against the agreed deterministic build behaviour and avoid competing task interpretations.
items.rationale: The reinstated refactor-change-record change owns a shared lazy-loaded record and next-action interpretation using lifecycle and artifact evidence.

items.description: Sidecar task plans are read sequentially when listing changes.
items.evidence: Each building abbreviated record is awaited during row construction; practical impact depends on workload.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Consider whether measured listing latency warrants concurrent reads, rather than adding concurrency speculatively.
items.rationale: No measured performance problem justifies introducing concurrency for these reads.

items.description: Activation refers to preparation mode without a clear entry point in abbreviated skills.
items.evidence: The owning skills describe a user request to prepare without execution, but activation has no explicit mechanism for passing that intent.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Make the preparation-only handoff explicit and ensure it returns to activation rather than executing or stopping ambiguously.
items.rationale: Explicitly define preparation-only invocation and return to activation before named build.

items.description: Prepare advertises activation while direct named bugfix/refactor invocation remains supported.
items.evidence: Different advertised and available entry points are not necessarily contradictory.
items.analysis: Review claims are evidence to assess; disposition is pending user decision.
items.recommendation: Clarify direct invocation only if the workflow is materially ambiguous; otherwise decline.
items.rationale: The remove-prepare-skill change will remove prepare and reconcile its callers and direct-entry guidance.

items.description: Unlinked sidecar work may remain in the checkout while normal activation continues.
items.evidence: Activation continues after a declined or unanswered link prompt; mixed work could later be included in a delivery.
items.analysis: Continuing normal work alongside unlinked active sidecar changes risks mixing work in a later delivery.
items.recommendation: Stop before progressing normal work when a concurrently active sidecar is unlinked, and explain independent work options.
items.rationale: Concurrent activation links automatically; independent delivery is allowed without auditing or automatically stashing work. Completion unlinks a surviving active sibling when only one is archived.

items.description: Concurrent builds of the same target can overwrite task work.
items.evidence: Two agents can read and modify the same files and task plan concurrently.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Assess whether concurrent builds of one target should be supported; locking adds coordination.
items.rationale: Concurrent builds of the same target in one worktree are outside the intended workflow; separate worktrees provide isolation.

items.description: Concurrent activations can overwrite the normal selector.
items.evidence: Selector check and write are separate operations.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Assess whether concurrent activation against one worktree is in scope.
items.rationale: Simultaneous independent activations in one worktree are outside the intended workflow; use separate worktrees.

items.description: Concurrent registry updates can lose entries.
items.evidence: Atomic replacement does not serialize concurrent read-modify-write operations.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Assess whether simultaneous mutations of one worktree registry are in scope.
items.rationale: Concurrent registry mutations by multiple agents in one worktree are outside the intended workflow.

items.description: A stopped sidecar activation can leave a new registry entry.
items.evidence: Activation registers before the prompt and can stop without invoking build, while policy says not to retain a new entry if work does not commence.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Ensure stopped activation removes only its newly added entry or register only after commencement.
items.rationale: Registration represents an activated sidecar; remove the link prompt and its declined/unanswered path. Registry cleanup follows completion or explicit local stop.

items.description: The changes CLI does not report the local sidecar registry.
items.evidence: The changes skill reads the registry, but _report_changes reads only durable records.
items.analysis: The CLI omits worktree-local sidecar registration and stale registry diagnostics.
items.recommendation: Decide whether the CLI should expose local activity and stale entries, or defer it to dedicated CLI work.
items.rationale: Expose registered local sidecars and stale registry entries through the changes CLI.

items.description: Branch completion removes registry entries before archival delivery is pushed.
items.evidence: Complete removes entries after the local archive mutation but before commit and push.
items.analysis: Completion only applies to delivered committed records; a local archive move alone is not the condition for ending local sidecar activity.
items.recommendation: Clarify the lifecycle point at which local sidecar activity ends and preserve retryability.
items.rationale: Remove a sidecar from current-sidecars when it is completed, not merely when its directory is archived; uncommitted or approved work cannot be completed. Cleanup must be retryable.

items.description: Cleanup retry after cancellation or direct completion is unclear.
items.evidence: The entry can remain after its change is archived, while cancel and direct-delivery complete reject archived targets.
items.analysis: Registry removal is driven by the complete event, independently of the directory being archived; the archive location is not the cleanup condition.
items.recommendation: Provide an explicit idempotent local registry cleanup path for archived records.
items.rationale: Make completion-triggered registry removal retryable regardless of archive location, without mutating archived records.

items.description: Recovery PR finalisation lacks explicit registry cleanup.
items.evidence: Only direct and original-open PR paths mention registry cleanup.
items.analysis: Completion-triggered cleanup must apply on the recovery path as on every completion path.
items.recommendation: Align recovery and resumption cleanup with the chosen lifecycle policy.
items.rationale: The complete event triggers sidecar registry removal irrespective of delivery path or archive location.

items.description: Fresh project initialisation does not add the sidecar registry ignore rule.
items.evidence: _local_runtime_ignore_contents currently requires only current-change and context.json; lifecycle guidance separately requires ensuring the new rule.
items.analysis: The repository ignore file already contains the rule, but new project initialisation does not add it.
items.recommendation: Assess whether init/update should install the rule in addition to the existing agent instruction.
items.rationale: Add the current-sidecars ignore rule to project initialisation while preserving existing ignore-file contents.

items.description: Concurrent sidecar and normal activation can miss a linking prompt.
items.evidence: Selector and registry reads can interleave across separate simultaneous agents.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Assess whether same-worktree concurrent activation needs explicit coordination.
items.rationale: Simultaneous independent activations in one worktree are outside the intended workflow.

items.description: The review disputes skipping design for S-sized work.
items.evidence: The current policy and prior explicit user decision intentionally allow S-sized work to proceed to tasks.
items.analysis: Assessment and disposition pending.
items.recommendation: Decline: the S-sized design skip is deliberate.
items.rationale: Skipping design for S-sized normal changes is an explicit prior decision reflected in lifecycle policy.
